concepts.learning_objective: Students will identify the visible changes that show a plant is growing.
Students will explain, from the three-pot activity, that plants need both sunlight and water to grow.

topics.title: Leaves: the food factories of plants

concepts.learning_objective: Students will state that plants make and store food as starch in their broad, flat, green leaves.
Students will describe the iodine test for starch in a leaf and the reason for decolourising the leaf.
Students will infer from variegated and coloured leaves that chlorophyll and sunlight are needed to make starch.

topics.title: Role of air and the products of photosynthesis

concepts.learning_objective: Students will explain, using the caustic soda experiment, that carbon dioxide from air is essential for making starch.
Students will interpret the water-plant experiment to show that oxygen is released during photosynthesis in light.
Students will write the word equation of photosynthesis and name its raw materials and products.
Students will identify stomata as tiny pores on the surface of leaves, seen in a stained leaf peel.
Students will explain how stomata allow carbon dioxide and oxygen to move in and out of leaves.
Students will explain that water and dissolved minerals move up from the roots to all parts through the xylem.
Students will explain that food made in leaves is carried to other parts through the phloem and may be stored there.
Students will describe the germinating-seed experiment and state that all parts of a plant respire.
Students will write the word equation of respiration and identify its reactants and products.
Students will analyse how photosynthesis and respiration together keep the exchange of gases balanced.
